memories.content: Link expected participant burden in each user study task to its corresponding mitigation strategy.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the prototype and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided during user study sessions.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately after collection.
Specify the equipment to be loaned to participants who lack necessary devices.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
HCI ethics reviewers verify that expected burdens and mitigation strategies correspond to each user study task.
Inform participants that the formative evaluation prototype is not a finished service.
Set an upper limit on cumulative task burden when requesting repeated evaluations from the same participant.
The author of this proposal tends to emphasize expected benefits of the prototype over participant burden.
In organizations where leaders or institutional staff handle recruitment, recruitment authority and academic or professional evaluation authority may be combined in the same role.
Place observational evidence or sources adjacent to claims regarding user needs or field effects.
Distinguish at the sentence level between facts already confirmed in the field and predictions to be examined in the user study.
Do not use verbs implying proof of causality if the design does not support causal inference.
Prioritize citations of recent systems and field research in rapidly changing HCI topics.
Explain the user or operational stakeholder needs that each design choice aims to address.
Support each important conclusion with the closest evidence that directly examined it.
Reviewers first check direct evidence placed closest to important conclusions.
Use field cases in which people completed tasks by working around existing tools as evidence for the need for the design.
Distinguish between problems reported by operational stakeholders and those directly observed by the researcher as separate forms of evidence.
Field breakdown logs can reveal both system failures and user adaptive behaviors, including their timing and conditions.
In field sites introducing new systems, formal procedures often coexist with existing manual routines for a period, making it difficult to isolate the effects of single design changes.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate dimensions of HCI work. The reference frame concentrates on participant protection, access, study burden, and recruitment power, while the compared frame concentrates on evidentiary discipline, field observations, causal restraint, and justification of design decisions. No scope-aligned overlap or contradiction is established.
